newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TENNIS-ROSSET STORMS INTO SECOND ROUND OF HONG KONG OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ROSSET STORMS INTO SECOND ROUND OF HONG KONG OPEN.

text.p: Switzerland's Marc Rosset swept past Nicolas Kiefer of Germany 6-2 6-2 in the first round of the Hong Kong Open on Monday.
The second seed hit five aces as he disposed of Kiefer, the world number 103, in just 54 minutes.
"I played a solid match and am just happy to win," said world number 18 Rosset. "Under the lights you see the ball late and that caused me to make some strange mistakes."
Rosset beat Kiefer on his way to winning the European Community championship in February -- his only tournament success so far this season..

He was joined in the second round by 20-year-old American Justin Gimelstob, who represented his country in this year's Hopman Cup with Chanda Rubin. Gimelstob defeated Sweden's Henrik Holm 1-6 7-6 6-2.

Holm, a former top 20 player who is on the comeback trail after a long layoff with an injured right shoulder, failed to convert three match points in the second set and ran out of ideas in the decider.
In the only other match on Monday, number eight seed Daniel Vacek of the Czech Republic defeated Alexander Volkov of Russia 6-4 7-6.
Top seed Michael Chang, twice a winner of the tournament, will play his first-round match on Tuesday against wild card entrant Melvin Tong of Hong Kong.
Chang was elevated to top seed after defending champion and world number one Pete Sampras withdrew last week with a wrist injury.
